intent: Hold the open state of one edge-anchored panel that the user can swipe away, and tie its trigger to that panel.
typical_uses: A focused task, form or filter set in a panel rising from the bottom edge that the user flicks away
A panel at a side edge whose drag and release are part of how it is dismissed

dont_use_when.situation: The same edge panel with no swipe gesture to dismiss it
A short prompt or form shown centered over the page
A confirmation the user must answer before continuing, such as before a destructive action
A floating panel anchored to its trigger that leaves the page interactive

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

`snapPoint` and `defaultSnapPoint` are both accepted; `defaultSnapPoint` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `snapPoint` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render. With neither, the first entry of `snapPoints` is used, and closing the drawer returns an uncontrolled snap point to that initial one.
`side` names the viewport edge the panel is pinned to and is passed to the primitive as the swipe direction that dismisses it (`top` as up, `bottom` as down, `left` and `right` unchanged).
`snapPoints` position the panel only when `side` is `top` or `bottom`; on a `left` or `right` drawer the primitive ignores them.

With `modal` at its default `true`, focus is trapped in the panel, page scroll is locked, presses outside the panel reach nothing on the page and DrawerContent draws its backdrop; `'trap-focus'` traps focus but neither locks page scroll, adds the primitive's own blocking layer nor draws the backdrop; `false` does none of these.

Escape, a press outside the panel and a swipe of the panel toward its edge past its last snap point, or past the edge when it has none, close the drawer, reporting the reason to `onOpenChange`; with nested dialogs or drawers open, Escape closes only the topmost one. `disablePointerDismissal` keeps an outside press from closing it, and for a non-modal drawer also keeps focus moving out from closing it.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Update the state `open` reads from inside `onOpenChange`; a controlled drawer closes only when `open` turns false, so Escape, an outside press, a swipe and every DrawerClose otherwise leave it open

children.states: children is the root's content, either React nodes or a function of the active trigger's payload that returns them
children.because: `React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` - the function form receives `{ payload }` from whichever trigger opened the drawer. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

modal.states: modal is true, false or the string 'trap-focus'
modal.because: `boolean | 'trap-focus'` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a boolean-or-string union is left unasserted.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (a trigger press, an outside press, Escape, a close press, a swipe, focus moving out or an imperative action). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<DrawerRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Drawer.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this root
handle.because: `DrawerHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the drawer's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled drawer is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open drawer is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

snapPoints.states: snapPoints lists the heights the panel can rest at - a number from 0 to 1 is a fraction of the viewport height, a larger number is pixels, and a string gives px or rem
snapPoints.because: `DrawerSnapPoint[]` where `DrawerSnapPoint` is `number | string` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so an array of a number-or-string union is left unasserted.

snapPoint.states: snapPoint is the active snap point, one of the values in snapPoints, or null
snapPoint.because: `number | string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so the union is left unasserted.

defaultSnapPoint.states: defaultSnapPoint is the snap point an uncontrolled drawer starts at, or null
defaultSnapPoint.because: `number | string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so the union is left unasserted.

onSnapPointChange.states: onSnapPointChange is a callback called with the next snap point and event details, not a value
onSnapPointChange.because: `(snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint | null, eventDetails) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

good.title: A bottom drawer opened by a kit Button, with a title and footer actions
good.code:
<Drawer>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit profile</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Edit profile</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Changes apply when you save.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
      <DrawerClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>

good.title: A controlled right-edge drawer with its grab bar shown

bad.title: The primitive's swipe direction passed to the root
bad.why: The kit's Drawer types no `swipeDirection` (the edge is `side`), so this fails type checking; at runtime it still reaches the primitive and overrides the direction `side` set, while DrawerContent keeps its border, axis and `data-side` for the default `bottom`, so the panel's position and its styling disagree.
